correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the universal degree-bound proof without coordinatization: for connected dominating D of k vertices in the 2v-vertex (q+1)-regular bipartite incidence graph, boundary edges satisfy 2v-k <= (q-1)k+2, giving k>=2(q+1). Equality forces G[D] to be a tree and every exterior vertex to have exactly one selected neighbor. A flag D(p,l) satisfies both by unique point joining and line meeting axioms. In any equality set, at least two selected points and lines; the unique exterior-neighbor property forces joining lines of every selected point pair and intersection points of every selected line pair into D. Noncollinear triples would generate an internal 6-cycle, so points are collinear and lines concurrent; domination fills the entire line and pencil, hence all equality sets are exactly flag double stars. Every exterior vertex then has exactly one forced tree attachment, giving a bijection with max-leaf spanning trees and exactly 2q^2 leaves. Intersections of two flag double stars have 2q+2-q= q+2 vertices for a common point/line and exactly two for flags sharing neither, implying exchange distances q or 2q, so the r=q graph is the line graph of the plane incidence graph with degree 2q. Incidence-graph diameter and non-crossed flags give line-graph radius=diameter=3 for all q>=2. Independently enumerated all 2^14 Fano-plane candidate subsets: precisely 21 size-six connected dominating sets; analytic proof handles every plane. Source two finite exhaustive scripts separately cover q=2 and q=3 but their outputs are not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The connected-domination/max-leaf equivalence is classical (Caro–West–Yuster). Goldberg–Rajendraprasad–Mathew and Héger–Nagy give ordinary (not necessarily connected) domination for projective-plane Levi graphs. Their q-level and small dominating-set classifications do not state the exact equality rigidity for connected domination, forced count of max-leaf trees or optimal batch-exchange threshold. The class includes non-Desarguesian planes, so no special automorphism argument is used. An inaccessible/unindexed exact Levi-graph connected-domination theorem remains a priority risk; do not equate search absence with certification.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a structural description of every minimizer of a natural graph-optimization problem on classical incidence geometries, not just a numerical bound. The exact max-leaf tree bijection and sharp q simultaneous-exchange barrier describe geometric rigidity and optimal reconfiguration for all existing projective planes, including non-Desarguesian cases. This is substantial motivated extremal graph theory.

final_claim: For every existing finite projective plane of order q>=2, all minimum connected dominating sets in its point–line incidence graph are exactly the incident-flag double stars, size 2(q+1), and count (q^2+q+1)(q+1). There is a unique maximum-leaf spanning tree per flag with 2q^2 leaves. Optimal simultaneous exchange is impossible for r<q, and at r=q the exchange graph equals the incidence-graph line graph, regular degree 2q and diameter/radius 3.
